return: The integer number of index-distinct triples of input values that can form a nondegenerate triangle. Equal-valued occurrences remain distinct choices; zero-length or equality-degenerate triples do not count. Fewer than three entries return 0.

numeric: Each two-side sum is at most 9007199254740990, so the triangle comparison is exact. The maximum count is choose(10000,3) = 166616670000; every added right-left and accumulating prefix stays within that bound. The JavaScript sort comparator uses relations and returns -1, 0 or 1, not subtraction.
complexity: Two-pointer counting takes O(n*n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary state after the sorted copy. JavaScript sorting adds T_sort(n) time and O(n+S_sort(n)) auxiliary space including the copied Array; ECMAScript does not impose universal sort complexity. For a fixed largest side, a successful left+right comparison validates all right-left possible smaller-left choices, and then decrements right; otherwise only left advances. No cubic triple enumeration is used.
